column4: The exact parallel قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ joins the section's two positive terms: attaining falah and purifying oneself.
Moses' warning وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ makes fabrication a pursuit whose maker returns deprived, exactly the section's خَابَ result.
وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا gives the section's empty-handed outcome to the person who arrives at judgment carrying wrongdoing.
وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ applies the section's خَابَ to the obstinate tyrant after the messengers seek victory.
وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِ makes purification accrue to one's own self, directly answering the section's self whose share is enlarged or diminished.
وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى names the most wretched as the one who actively avoids the reminder, the negative seeker described in the section.
لَا يَصْلَىٰهَا إِلَّا ٱلْأَشْقَى repeats the section's superlative ٱلْأَشْقَى and gives that person's final destination.
فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِىٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ makes the judgment-day division between the wretched and the happy explicit, matching the section's two opposed outcomes.
The condemned confess رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا; wretchedness has overcome them and brought their striving to its failed end.
قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ repeats the section's emphatic قَدْ أَفْلَحَ construction and opens a concrete account of those who attain the good sought.
فَيَنقَلِبُوا خَائِبِينَ depicts the defeated party turning back disappointed, a direct scene of returning without the object sought.
أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ uses the section's d-s-s/d-s-w word family in its concrete sense of hiding a child in the earth, exposing the violence within the image of burying a self.
مَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰ uses the section's sh-q-w word for hardship and explicitly denies that the revelation was sent to exhaust its recipient.
Adam is warned that expulsion from the garden will leave him فَتَشْقَىٰ, illustrating the section's secondary sense of sh-q-w as toil and hardship.
فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ promises that following divine guidance prevents both losing the way and ending in wretchedness.
Zechariah says he has never been بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا: his seeking through prayer has not ended in deprivation, joining the section's search and sh-q-w senses.
Abraham hopes not to be بِدُعَاءِ رَبِّى شَقِيًّا, again using sh-q-w for a petitioner's feared failure to obtain what he seeks.
Jesus says God did not make him جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا; the pairing of tyrant and wretched directly meets the section's quoted tyrant who خَابَ in 14:15.
فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُوا۟ places the wretched group of 11:105 in the Fire, supplying the first outcome of that ayah's division.
سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ identifies the receptive seeker as the one who fears and takes the reminder, the positive half of the section's quoted division.
ٱلَّذِى يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ gives the most wretched person's avoidance in 87:11 its fiery result.
ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ makes failed striving end in a state that is neither death nor life, completing the consequence begun in 87:11-12.
وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ supplies remembrance and prayer as the acts accompanying the purification and falah of 87:14.
بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا identifies preference for the nearer life as the rival pursuit immediately after the falah statement.
وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ makes the better object also the one that remains, sharpening the section's definition of falah as remaining in good.
إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ announces divergent strivings, an exact structural parallel to the section's two searches and their different ends.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ gives the generous, God-fearing believer's pursuit a course toward ease.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ gives the denying, self-sufficient person's pursuit a course toward hardship, the section's labor that ends in depletion.
وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ shows the failed seeker discovering that accumulated wealth supplies nothing at the fall.
فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ introduces the blaze into which 92:15 places the most wretched.
ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ defines the most wretched of 92:15 by denial and turning away, matching the avoider of the reminder in 87:11.
ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُۥ يَتَزَكَّىٰ places self-purification on the opposite trajectory from the most wretched person's fire.
إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ states the purified giver's sought object: the face of his Lord Most High.
وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ closes that directed search with attainment and satisfaction rather than an empty hand.
ٱبْتَغُوا۟ إِلَيْهِ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ ... لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ explicitly connects seeking a way, exertion, and falah.
Those who يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ are called ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, so the object consciously sought and the attainment of falah meet in one ayah.
فَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ ... لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ joins seeking provision, remembering God, and attaining falah.
أُو۟لَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثُونَ begins to specify what the successful believers of 23:1 actually receive.
ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ defines their attainment as inheriting Paradise and remaining there, the section's lexical account of falah made scene.
Those whose scales are heavy are هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ; falah is pictured as arriving at judgment with real weight rather than a diminished share.
Those whose scales are light خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُم, a concrete negative counterpart to 7:8 and to the section's person who lowers his own self's portion.
Heavy scales again identify هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, placing falah in the judgment scene that soon contains the confession of wretchedness in 23:106.
Light scales mean خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ, directly staging the self as the thing the failed person has lost.
وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ locates the obstacle and the rescue within the self, as this section does.
The repeated formula about being guarded from شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ and becoming ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ again makes treatment of one's self determine the attained result.
Eternal gardens are called جَزَاءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ, giving purification the lasting good that the section hears in falah.
هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا asks for the people whose work has produced the greatest loss, directly opening the section's image of strenuous failure.
ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ ... وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا depicts effort going astray while its doers suppose they are achieving well.
عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ pictures faces whose labor has only exhausted them, the closest nonlexical parallel to the section's most strenuous person ending depleted.
تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً gives the exhausted labor of 88:3 its destination in fire.
Whoever seeks ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ receives only what God hastens for whom He wills and then reaches Hell, a precise failed pursuit of the nearer life.
Whoever seeks the Hereafter and makes its proper striving has سَعْيُهُم مَّشْكُورًا, the positive pursuit opposed to futile exhaustion.
The two seekers desire different harvests; the seeker of the world receives some of it but has no نَصِيبٍ in the Hereafter, exactly the section's diminished share.
The person who asks only for this world has وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ, a seeker left with no portion in the enduring life.
The second petitioner seeks good in both lives and protection from the Fire, supplying the rightly directed search beside 2:200.
أُو۟لَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ answers the section's diminished portion with a share resulting from what these seekers earned.
Those who desire worldly life and its adornment are paid their deeds there وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يُبْخَسُونَ, setting up a pursuit fully paid only in the wrong domain.
In the Hereafter those worldly seekers have only the Fire, and وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ makes their labor finally empty.
وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ makes what a person obtains answer directly to what the person strove for.
وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُۥ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ promises that the striving itself will be brought into view rather than disappear unnoticed.
ثُمَّ يُجْزَىٰهُ ٱلْجَزَاءَ ٱلْأَوْفَىٰ completes the sequence with full recompense, the opposite of a shrunken share.
إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ makes every human a laboring seeker who will meet the Lord and the result of that labor.
وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَّشْكُورًا tells the people of Paradise that their striving was appreciated, a direct counter-image to effort ending fruitless.
Moses asks Pharaoh هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ, presenting purification as a path Pharaoh may choose rather than the burying of his self.
وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ joins guidance toward the Lord with fear, the same receptive stance as 87:10.
يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مَا سَعَىٰ places remembered striving before the final two-way division.
فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ identifies transgression as the first course whose result follows.
وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats 87:16's preference for the nearer life as the failed seeker's choice.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ gives that preference its attained destination.
The other person fears standing before the Lord and restrains ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ, treating the self in the opposite way from burying it under desire.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the lasting destination of the disciplined self.
لَعَلَّهُۥ يَزَّكَّىٰ presents purification as the possible outcome for the blind seeker who has come for instruction.
أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ joins remembrance and benefit exactly as the reminder passage in 87:9-10 does.
وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ makes the self-sufficient listener's failure to purify himself his own outcome.
وَأَمَّا مَن جَآءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ makes the receptive person literally come striving, a concrete seeker within the reminder scene.
وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ gives that striver the fear that characterizes the one who remembers in 87:10.
فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ records the seeker being overlooked, sharpening the passage's question of who receives the reminder.
A thirsty person pursues a mirage, then لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْـًٔا: this is the section's empty-handed seeker rendered as a complete Quranic scene.
The following layered darkness ends وَمَن لَّمْ يَجْعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ, matching the section's hand left without a spark or light.
The rejecters' deeds become ashes driven by wind, and لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ makes their earnings unobtainable.

فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءًۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ distinguishes what vanishes uselessly from what benefits and remains, the section's two results in physical form.
مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ states directly that one possession runs out while the other remains, clarifying falah as continuance in good.
ٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ are better in reward and hope, uniting lasting good with the seeker's expectation of an outcome.
Those who forget God are made to forget أَنفُسَهُمْ, a direct inner parallel to suppressing and losing one's own self.
إِنَّ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ makes the self itself the decisive loss on judgment day.
Deeds are turned هَبَآءً مَّنثُورًا, a visible counterpart to exertion that yields no retained good.
بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ shows a person's own earnings coating and dimming the heart, close to the section's self made obscure by its possessor.
The person kindles a fire, then God takes نُورِهِمْ and leaves them in darkness; the fire succeeds physically but its seekers are left without its light.
Hypocrites ask believers for light and are told فَٱلْتَمِسُوا۟ نُورًا behind them; their too-late search for light ends at a barrier.
فَٱلْمُورِيَٰتِ قَدْحًا stages successful striking that throws sparks, directly illuminating the section's dictionary image of a qadh that is rubbed but will not spark.
Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring a قَبَسٍ or find guidance at it, a seeker approaching light with a stated object.
فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ shows that Moses' fire-search does reach something: at arrival he receives the divine call.
Moses sees a fire and promises either news or بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ, repeating the concrete search for a usable flame.
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ makes arrival at the fire yield a call and blessing, more than the ember initially sought.
Moses hopes to return from the distant fire with news or جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ, another direct fire-seeking scene.
فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ completes the search: reaching the fire becomes the site of revelation.
أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى تُورُونَ addresses people about the fire they kindle, the successful act reversed in the section's non-sparking stick.
The question whether humans produced شَجَرَتَهَا locates the kindled fire in its tree, the material counterpart to the section's fire-stick.
God makes that fire تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَٰعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ: unlike the useless stick, it gives reminder and provision to travelers.
The criminal in Hell لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ exactly repeats 87:13's result for the most wretched person.
خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا gives the wretched group a terrible continuance, showing that mere duration differs from the section's falah of remaining in good.
Immediately after confessing their wretchedness, the condemned ask to be taken out and promise righteousness if returned; even their new search is now too late.
ٱخْسَـُٔوا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ refuses that request, leaving the failed seekers without the exit they seek.
وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ directs the seeker's resources toward the enduring home while retaining a proper worldly share.
People who had wished for Qarun's place discover that provision is measured by God and conclude لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ, a corrected worldly search ending in a falah judgment.
Those who follow ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُ are هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, directly joining the light missing from the failed fire-stick with falah.
Pharaoh's magicians claim وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ; their falah means gaining worldly ascendancy, a pointed rival sense to remaining in moral good.
The righteous believer need not fear ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا, an explicit protection from injustice or diminution opposite the section's self whose share is made small.
وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَتْقَى reverses 92:15: the most God-fearing is kept away from the fire entered by the most wretched.
Opposite those who شَقُوا۟, the happy remain in the Garden and receive عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, a gift never cut off that realizes lasting good.
فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ draws a boundary between actually purifying the self and claiming purity for oneself; God best knows who is mindful.
Those who يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم are corrected with بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ, distinguishing self-praise from the purification tied to falah.
مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا without God's grace places divine enabling around the section's human act of purifying the self.
A person made alive and given نُورًا يَمْشِى بِهِ contrasts with one trapped in darkness, reversing the section's dimmed self and lightless hand.
Believing men and women have their light running before them; this is the attained light that the hypocrites of 57:13 seek only after it is inaccessible.
God makes fire from ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ so that people kindle from it, a concrete reversal of the section's stick that yields no spark.
The lasting home is for those who do not seek عُلُوًّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ; this corrects the magicians' claim in 20:64 that success belongs to whoever rises highest.
Those who strive for God are promised guidance into His ways, showing exertion that opens a path rather than ending in exhausted deprivation.
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِى كَبَدٍ makes toil a general human condition, supporting the section's explicit boundary that not every fatigue is wretchedness.
فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ commands renewed exertion, a positive case of tiring effort rather than the futile labor attached to wretchedness.
وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب directs desire to its true object, making the positive exertion of 94:7 a purposeful search.
فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ is the command that creates the reminder scene divided between the fearful hearer and the avoider in 87:10-11.
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَٰشِعَةٌ introduces the abased faces whose next description is laboring and exhausted; its own contribution is their final humiliation.
مِّن وَرَآئِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ gives the failed tyrant of 14:15 what lies ahead and begins to specify what his empty-handed end contains.
Death comes to the tyrant from every side وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ, extending his failure into an existence that cannot even reach death.
Receiving the record in the right hand begins the favorable result for the laborer who must meet his Lord in 84:6.
Receiving the record from behind the back begins the contrary result for the same universal labor described in 84:6.
فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوا۟ ثُبُورًا shows the unsuccessful laborer calling for destruction when the result is received.
وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا completes that laborer's result in a blaze, paralleling the exhausted faces of 88:3-4.
وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ calls each self to inspect what it has sent ahead, immediately before 59:19's self-forgetting failure.
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ restates with falah vocabulary the section's 20:61 claim that the fabricator خَابَ.
Those who fabricate lawful and unlawful against God لَا يُفْلِحُونَ, another concrete meeting of false invention with failed attainment.
The command to act toward one's position ends with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ, connecting the eventual outcome with the wrongdoing borne by the failed person in 20:111.
Moses says God knows who receives the good final home and that wrongdoers do not attain falah, joining moral burden to final result.
If the cave companions are forced back into their people's religion, وَلَن تُفْلِحُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًا; falah here is enduring fidelity rather than momentary survival.
Those established عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ are ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, giving the section's idea of remaining in good the stable ground of guidance.
The repeated pairing عَلَىٰ هُدًى ... هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ again pictures falah as continuance upon guidance.
ٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ are better in reward and return, a repeated formulation of the good that remains and yields the better end.
Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment, while مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ identifies the better and more lasting object.
Whatever people receive is only worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ for believers who trust Him.
The person who worships on an edge turns back under trial and خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةَ, a pursuit that loses both the near and lasting goods.
مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ says acquired wealth and earnings avail nothing, close to the fruitless accumulation of 92:11.
سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ gives the unavailing earnings of 111:2 their fiery outcome.
Earlier peoples enjoyed their خَلَاق, but their deeds became void and they became the losers; the ayah connects a consumed share with wasted work.
Ostentatious charity is like soil washed from smooth rock, leaving it bare; the givers retain nothing مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟.
A fruitful garden is struck by a fiery whirlwind when its owner is vulnerable, a concrete image of long labor yielding nothing at the moment it is needed.
Wrongdoers' expenditure is likened to a freezing wind that destroys a crop, so apparent provision and effort leave no harvest.
Those who desire worldly life see Qarun's display and wish for his portion, establishing the mistaken search corrected in 28:82.
People of knowledge answer that God's reward is better for belief and righteous action, naming the better object of pursuit.
The earth swallows Qarun and his home, making the admired worldly attainment vanish before the wishers' eyes.
بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ repeats the preference for the immediate life that marks the failed trajectory in 87:16 and 17:18.
وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ states what is abandoned when the immediate life becomes the sought object.
إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَآءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا gives the same pursuit its neglected consequence.
أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ questions satisfaction with the nearer life when its enjoyment is little beside the lasting one.
Believers ask رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا after sincere repentance, a successful orientation toward the light absent from the section's failed hand.
The buried girl is brought forward and questioned; this may echo the section's literalized idea of a buried self, though the ayah concerns a murdered child rather than inward concealment.
بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ exposes the guilt behind literal burial; the link to burying one's own self is analogical and the actors differ.
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ gives generosity and God-consciousness as the first acts on the striving that is eased toward ease in 92:7.
وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ supplies affirmation of the best promise as the positive seeker's orientation before the result in 92:7.
وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ names stinginess and imagined self-sufficiency as the acts on the striving eased toward hardship in 92:10.
وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ gives denial of the best promise as the failed seeker's orientation before the result in 92:10.
وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ clarifies that the purified giver's expenditure is not repayment of a human favor, preparing 92:20's sole sought object.
وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ is the promise of ease immediately before the command to remind, anticipating the two courses toward ease and hardship in Surah 92.
أَمَّا مَنِ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ identifies the self-sufficient person who receives attention, the contrary figure to the fearful seeker who comes striving.
فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ records attention being directed to the self-sufficient listener, completing the interpersonal reversal exposed by 80:8-10.
The people whose striving went astray denied their Lord's signs and meeting, so their works became void and have no weight at judgment.
Hell is the recompense for the people of 18:103-105, completing the account of where their seemingly good workmanship actually leads.
The exhausted faces are made to drink from a boiling spring, specifying what their labor has obtained.
Their only food is bitter thorn, another concrete yield of labor that ended in wretchedness.
لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِن جُوعٍ makes that food neither nourish nor relieve hunger, an exact image of receiving something that supplies no good.
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاعِمَةٌ opens the opposite judgment scene to the abased, exhausted faces of 88:2-3.
لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ reverses the fruitless labor of 88:3: these faces are satisfied with the result of their striving.
فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ gives the satisfied striving of 88:9 its lasting destination.
فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا gives the right-hand recipient an easy accounting, the favorable result of the universal labor in 84:6.
وَيَنقَلِبُ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِۦ مَسْرُورًا makes that seeker return joyfully, opposite the disappointed return captured by خَائِبِينَ in 3:127.
Fire scorches the faces of those whose light scales meant loss of self, specifying the bodily consequence before their confession in 23:106.
The condemned are asked whether God's signs were recited and rejected; their failure to receive the reminder explains the wretchedness confessed next.
A group of believers had prayed for forgiveness and mercy, introducing the people whose patient seeking receives the contrary result in 23:111.
The condemned mocked those petitioners until mockery made them forget God's remembrance, showing how their own conduct obscured the self.
إِنِّى جَزَيْتُهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ gives patient believers attained victory opposite the confessing wretched group.
وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ brings the result into sight between remembering one's striving and the division of the two seekers.
فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ repeats the heavy-scale side of the judgment image that associates an undiminished share with success.
فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ gives the person of heavy scales a satisfying life, the good attained and retained.
وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ repeats the light-scale side, concretizing the section's self whose portion has been made small.
فَأُمُّهُۥ هَاوِيَةٌ gives the light-scale person an abyss as the destination reached.
وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا هِيَهْ holds open the identity of that abyss before the next ayah names it.
نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ identifies the abyss reached by the person of light scales as a blazing fire.
Whoever desires the reward of this world receives from it, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter receives from it; the ayah states the section's two searches in parallel.
مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا is reminded that with God are the rewards of both world and Hereafter, correcting a search narrowed to the nearer return.
مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ identifies the two desired objects amid a battle where disobedience has already changed the outcome.
كُلًّا نُّمِدُّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مِنْ عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَ says both kinds of seeker in 17:18-19 receive worldly supply, while their final results still diverge.
Good spent while seeking God's face is for the giver's own self and will be repaid fully, joining the sought object, self-benefit, and an undiminished result.
Spending for God's pleasure and from inner firmness is like a garden yielding doubled produce, the fruitful reversal of the bare rock in 2:264.
Charity given while seeking God's face makes its givers ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ, an enlarged return opposite the section's self whose share is diminished.
The command not to trade God's covenant for a small price says what is with God is better, preparing 16:96's contrast between what perishes and what remains.
The passing bloom of worldly life is set against رِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ, identifying the better and more lasting provision.
The command to persevere in prayer is joined to نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ and وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ, connecting sustained effort, provision, and final outcome.
The failed seekers of light are told that they tempted their own selves, waited, doubted, and were deceived by wishes; the ayah locates their dark result in self-directed acts.
No ransom is accepted from the failed light-seekers and the Fire becomes their refuge, completing the barred search of 57:13-14.
This single ayah joins faith written in hearts, gardens in which believers remain, God's pleasure, and the verdict that God's party are ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ.
The person who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs is told that wrongdoers do not attain falah, combining the two failed types quoted in 20:61 and 20:111.
Fabricating against God or denying His signs ends with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ, restating the section's fabricator who returns deprived.
Joseph rejects the invited betrayal with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ, giving wrongdoing a concrete temptation and a failed result.
The command to all believers to turn back to God ends لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ, presenting repentance as a directed course toward falah.
Repentance, belief, and righteous action make a person likely to be among ٱلْمُفْلِحِينَ, specifying a repaired course for the self.
Patience, mutual steadfastness, watchful constancy, and God-consciousness lead to لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ, giving falah the sustained action suggested by remaining in good.
Charity is taken to cleanse and وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا, showing purification and growth enacted through a concrete gift.
Lowering the gaze and guarding chastity is ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ, a specific practice by which a self becomes purer.
وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا makes each self bear the result of its own earning, reinforcing 35:18's self-directed purification.
لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ assigns each self its acquired good and incurred evil, the section's two self-produced shares.
إِنْ أَحْسَنتُمْ أَحْسَنتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا makes good and harm return to the acting selves.
مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِۦ وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا repeats the precise self-benefit and self-harm relation developed in the section.
The same formula makes righteous action accrue to one's own self and evil fall against it before all return to their Lord.
God does not change a people's condition until they change what is in their own selves, a specific account of inward action producing the attained condition.
God does not alter a favor given to a people until they alter what is in their selves, connecting inward corruption with a diminished provision.
فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓا۟ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ makes an initial self-chosen deviation end in further distortion of the heart.
Those who trade God's covenant and oaths for a small price have no share in the Hereafter, a direct scene of choosing diminution and ending deprived.
The ayah calls worldly enjoyment little, the Hereafter better for the God-conscious, and promises they will not be wronged even by a thread-like amount.
Every thirst, fatigue, hunger, and step endured in God's path is recorded as a righteous deed; this concretely proves the section's boundary that fatigue need not be wretchedness or wasted effort.
God answers that He does not let the work of any worker be lost, then promises expiation and gardens to those who bore exile and harm.
For the believer who does righteous deeds there is no rejection of striving—فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ—and it is recorded, directly reversing futile effort.
The command to cast كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ into Hell supplies a repeated obstinate figure and destination for the عَنِيد whose failure the section quotes from 14:15.
Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has attained success, while worldly life is only deceptive enjoyment.
Those who fear their Lord receive gardens in which they remain forever and mutual pleasure with God, extending the fearful recipient of 87:10 into a lasting result.
Worldly life is pictured as rain-grown vegetation that impresses, withers, yellows, and becomes debris, a concrete account of the sought good that does not remain.
سَابِقُوٓا۟ directs a race toward forgiveness and a garden, turning the enduring result into an explicitly pursued goal.

God holds people to account whether they reveal or conceal what is within their selves; this may bound the section's self-concealment by showing that inward hiding cannot remove its contents from divine knowledge.
God knows what people hide in their breasts and what they reveal; the link is an indirect boundary on the section's image of suppressing the self rather than the same act.
On the day of presentation no hidden thing remains hidden; this may reverse the buried-self image, though the ayah concerns exposure at judgment rather than self-purification.
